1.title: Pure Mathematics
1.lesson: Preserve exact structure where it exists, but encode non-reducibility and analogy as legitimate semantic outcomes.

13.title: Probability Theory
13.lesson: Make uncertainty typed: distributions, normalization, expectation, covariance, concentration and Markov evolution must carry probabilistic constraints.

15.title: Computational Mathematics
15.lesson: Numerical meaning requires error, conditioning and exactness metadata; algorithms should expose structured factorization rather than hide it.

17.title: Optimization
17.lesson: Optimization should be expressed through objective, constraints, regularity, duality and admission conditions rather than opaque search.

19.title: Decision Theory
19.lesson: Decisions require utility, risk, beliefs and uncertainty to remain visible; descriptive nonlinearity should not be silently linearized.

20.title: Game Theory
20.lesson: Multi-agent semantics require payoff structure, strategic state and equilibrium status, while computational hardness remains an explicit boundary.

21.title: Classical Mechanics
21.lesson: Dynamics should carry state, conserved quantities, energy and evolution operators, with exact and linearized regimes separated.

22.title: Continuum Mechanics
22.lesson: Tensor state and constitutive laws need symmetry, positivity and deformation-regime contracts.

23.title: Coupled Mechanics
23.lesson: Coupling belongs in first-class block relations; reciprocity, off-diagonal strength and thermodynamic admissibility should be inspectable.

27.title: Statistical Mechanics
27.lesson: Statistical state should expose ensembles, spectra, covariance, fluctuation and equilibrium/non-equilibrium regime.

32.title: Quantum Mechanics
32.lesson: Vector/operator/tensor-product semantics can be exact and should not be degraded into generic scalar plumbing.

57.title: Computational Neuroscience
57.lesson: Learned systems are often linear operators wrapped by nonlinear gates; adaptation should be represented as explicit update rules.

58.title: Computer Science
58.lesson: A language must represent algorithmic and combinatorial limits honestly; undecidability and complexity are semantic properties, not compiler failures.

59.title: Data Science
59.lesson: Data semantics need metrics, embeddings, spectra, clustering objectives and explicit nonlinear boundaries.

60.title: Machine Learning
60.lesson: Learning should expose objectives, regularization, Jacobians, backpropagation and model-update provenance.

61.title: Artificial Intelligence
61.lesson: Reasoning mixes combinatorial search, probabilistic inference, contraction/value updates and matrix-based learned models; each regime should remain distinguishable.

62.title: Robotics
62.lesson: Transform, Jacobian, estimation, planning and control semantics should be typed with local capability and uncertainty.

77.title: Network Science
77.lesson: Graphs are native algebraic objects: adjacency, Laplacian, spectra, paths and communities should not be encoded as untyped arrays.

79.title: Information Theory
79.lesson: Information is measurable state: entropy, divergence, channel and code structure should be first-class with exactness and capacity bounds.

80.title: Parallel and Distributed Computing
80.lesson: Parallel execution needs work, communication, memory, scheduling and impossibility contracts; backendless execution may model distribution without opening a network.
